A rotation requires knowing the center (point) and the measure/direction of the angle of rotation. A line reflection requires a line and the knowledge of perpendicular bisectors.

domain: Geometry - Similarity, Right Triangles and Trigonometry (GEO-G.SRT)
skill: Establish AA, SSS, SAS similarity criteria
description: Use the properties of similarity transformations to establish the AA~, SSS~, and SAS~ criterion for two triangles to be similar.

domain: Geometry - Similarity, Right Triangles and Trigonometry (GEO-G.SRT)
skill: Prove and apply similarity theorems about triangles
description: Prove and apply similarity theorems about triangles. Notes: Include multi-step proofs and algebraic problems built upon these concepts. Examples of theorems include but are not limited to: If a line parallel to one side of a triangle intersects the other two sides of the triangle, then the line divides these two sides proportionally (and conversely). The length of the altitude drawn from the vertex of the right angle of a right triangle to its hypotenuse is the geometric mean between the lengths of the two segments of the hypotenuse. The centroid of the triangle divides each median in the ratio 2:1.

domain: Geometry - Similarity, Right Triangles and Trigonometry (GEO-G.SRT)
skill: Solve problems with congruence/similarity criteria
description: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to solve problems algebraically and geometrically. Notes: ASA, SAS, SSS, AAS, and Hypotenuse-Leg (HL) theorems are valid criteria for triangle congruence. AA~, SAS~, and SSS~ are valid criteria for triangle similarity. This standard is a fluency recommendation for Geometry.

domain: Geometry - Similarity, Right Triangles and Trigonometry (GEO-G.SRT)
skill: Prove relationships using congruence/similarity criteria
description: Use congruence and similarity criteria for triangles to prove relationships in geometric figures. Notes: ASA, SAS, SSS, AAS, and Hypotenuse-Leg (HL) theorems are valid criteria for triangle congruence. AA~, SAS~, and SSS~ are valid criteria for triangle similarity. This standard is a fluency recommendation for Geometry.

domain: Geometry - Similarity, Right Triangles and Trigonometry (GEO-G.SRT)
skill: Define trigonometric ratios from similarity
description: Understand that by similarity, side ratios in right triangles are properties of the angles in the triangle, leading to definitions of sine, cosine and tangent ratios for acute angles.

domain: Geometry - Similarity, Right Triangles and Trigonometry (GEO-G.SRT)
skill: Relate sine/cosine of complementary angles
description: Explain and use the relationship between the sine and cosine of complementary angles.

domain: Geometry - Similarity, Right Triangles and Trigonometry (GEO-G.SRT)
skill: Solve right triangles using trig ratios
description: Use sine, cosine, tangent, the Pythagorean Theorem and properties of special right triangles to solve right triangles in applied problems. ★ Note: Special right triangles refer to the 30-60-90 and 45-45-90 triangles.

domain: Geometry - Similarity, Right Triangles and Trigonometry (GEO-G.SRT)
skill: Find area of a triangle using sine formula
description: Justify and apply the formula A = (1/2)ab sin(C) to find the area of any triangle by drawing an auxiliary line from a vertex perpendicular to the opposite side.

skill: Prove all circles are similar
description: Prove that all circles are similar.

skill: Identify relationships between angles and intercepted arcs
description: Identify, describe and apply relationships between the angles and their intercepted arcs of a circle.

skill: Identify relationships among radii, chords, tangents, secants
description: Identify, describe and apply relationships among radii, chords, tangents, and secants of a circle. Note: These relationships that pertain to the circle may be utilized to prove other relationships in geometric figures, e.g., the opposite angles in any quadrilateral inscribed in a circle are supplements of each other. Also includes algebraic problems built upon these concepts.

skill: Use proportionality for arc length and sector area
description: Using proportionality, find one of the following given two others: the central angle, arc length, radius or area of sector. Note: Angle measure is in degrees.

domain: Geometry - Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations (GEO-G.GPE)
skill: Derive and find equation of a circle
description: Derive the equation of a circle of given center and radius using the Pythagorean Theorem. Find the center and radius of a circle, given the equation of the circle. Notes: Finding the center and radius may involve completing the square. The completing the square expectation for Geometry follows Algebra I: leading coefficients will be 1 (after possible removal of GCF) and the coefficients of the linear terms will be even. Completing the square may yield a fractional radius.

domain: Geometry - Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations (GEO-G.GPE)
skill: Graph circles given their equation
description: Graph circles given their equation. Note: For circles being graphed, the center will be an ordered pair of integers and the radius a positive integer.

domain: Geometry - Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations (GEO-G.GPE)
skill: Algebraically prove geometric theorems on coordinate plane
description: On the coordinate plane, algebraically prove geometric theorems and properties. Notes: Examples include but not limited to: Given points and/or characteristics, prove or disprove a polygon is a specified quadrilateral or triangle based on its properties. Given a point that lies on a circle with a given center, prove or disprove that a specified point lies on the same circle. This standard is a fluency recommendation for Geometry.

domain: Geometry - Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations (GEO-G.GPE)
skill: Explore proof of parallel/perpendicular slope relationship
description: On the coordinate plane, explore the proof for the relationship between slopes of parallel and perpendicular lines. Note: This standard is a fluency recommendation for Geometry.

domain: Geometry - Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations (GEO-G.GPE)
skill: Determine if lines are parallel/perpendicular by slope
description: On the coordinate plane, determine if lines are parallel, perpendicular, or neither, based on their slopes.

domain: Geometry - Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations (GEO-G.GPE)
skill: Apply parallel/perpendicular line properties to problems
description: On the coordinate plane, apply properties of parallel and perpendicular lines to solve geometric problems.

domain: Geometry - Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations (GEO-G.GPE)
skill: Find point that partitions a segment in a given ratio
description: Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the segment in a given ratio. Note: Midpoint formula is a derivative of this standard.

domain: Geometry - Expressing Geometric Properties with Equations (GEO-G.GPE)
skill: Use coordinates for perimeter and area
description: Use coordinates to compute perimeters of polygons and areas of triangles and rectangles. ★ Note: This standard is a fluency recommendation for Geometry.

skill: Give informal arguments for volume/area formulas
description: Provide informal arguments for the formulas for the circumference of a circle, area of a circle, volume of a cylinder, pyramid, and cone.

skill: Use volume formulas to solve problems
description: Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to solve problems. ★

skill: Identify cross-sections and rotational solids
description: Identify the shapes of plane sections of three-dimensional objects, and identify three-dimensional objects generated by rotations of two-dimensional objects. Note: Plane sections are not limited to being parallel or perpendicular to the base.

skill: Use geometric shapes to model objects
description: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe objects. ★

skill: Apply density concepts in modeling
description: Apply concepts of density based on area and volume of geometric figures in modeling situations. ★

skill: Apply geometric methods to design problems
description: Apply geometric methods to solve design problems. ★ Note: Applications may include designing an object or structure to satisfy constraints such as area, volume, mass and cost.

skill: Count to 100 by ones and tens
description: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.

skill: Count to 100 from any given number
description: Count to 100 by ones beginning from any given number (instead of beginning at 1).

skill: Write numbers 0 to 20
description: Write numbers from 0 to 20. Represent a number of objects with a written numeral 0-20 (with 0 representing a count of no objects).

skill: Use 1:1 correspondence when counting
description: When counting objects, say the number names in the standard order, pairing each object with one and only one number name and each number name with one and only one object. (1:1 correspondence)

skill: Understand cardinality
description: Understand that the last number name said tells the number of objects counted, (cardinality). The number of objects is the same regardless of their arrangement or the order in which they were counted.

skill: Understand each successive number is one larger
description: Understand the concept that each successive number name refers to a quantity that is one larger.

skill: Understand ordinal numbers first through tenth
description: Understand the concept of ordinal numbers (first through tenth) to describe the relative position and magnitude of whole numbers.

skill: Answer counting questions up to 20 objects
description: Answer counting questions using as many as 20 objects arranged in a line, a rectangular array, and a circle. Answer counting questions using as many as 10 objects in a scattered configuration. e.g., “How many ______ are there?”

skill: Count out a given number of objects
description: Given a number from 1–20, count out that many objects.

skill: Compare number of objects in two groups
description: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than (more than), less than (fewer than), or equal to (the same as) the number of objects in another group. Note: Include groups with up to ten objects. e.g., using matching and counting strategies

skill: Compare two numbers 1-10 as numerals
description: Compare two numbers between 1 and 10 presented as written numerals. e.g., 6 is greater than 2

skill: Represent addition and subtraction
description: Represent addition and subtraction using objects, fingers, pennies, drawings, sounds, acting out situations, verbal explanations, expressions, equations, or other strategies. Note: Drawings need not show details, but should show the mathematics in the problem.

skill: Add and subtract within 10
description: Add and subtract within 10.

skill: Solve addition/subtraction word problems within 10
description: Solve addition and subtraction word problems within 10. e.g., using objects or drawings to represent the problem

skill: Decompose numbers up to 10 into pairs
description: Decompose numbers less than or equal to 10 into pairs in more than one way. e.g., using objects or drawings. Record each decomposition with a drawing or equation. e.g., 5 = 2 + 3 and 5 = 4 + 1

skill: Find the number that makes 10
description: Find the number that makes 10 when given a number from 1 to 9. e.g., using objects or drawings. Record the answer with a drawing or equation.

skill: Fluently add and subtract within 5
description: Fluently add and subtract within 5.

skill: Duplicate, extend, create simple patterns
description: Duplicate, extend, and create simple patterns using concrete objects.

domain: Number and Operations in Base Ten (NY-K.NBT)
skill: Compose/decompose numbers 11-19
description: Compose and decompose the numbers from 11 to 19 into ten ones and one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, or nine ones. e.g., using objects or drawings

skill: Describe measurable attributes
description: Describe measurable attributes of an object(s), such as length or weight, using appropriate vocabulary. e.g., small, big, short, tall, empty, full, heavy, and light

skill: Directly compare two objects
description: Directly compare two objects with a common measurable attribute and describe the difference.

skill: Classify objects and count by category
description: Classify objects into given categories; count the objects in each category and sort the categories by count. Note: Limit category counts to be less than or equal to 10.

skill: Explore coins, identify pennies and dimes
description: Explore coins (pennies, nickels, dimes, and quarters) and begin identifying pennies and dimes.

skill: Describe objects using shape names and position
description: Describe objects in the environment using names of shapes, and describe the relative positions of these objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, and next to.

skill: Name shapes regardless of orientation/size
description: Name shapes regardless of their orientation or overall size.

skill: Understand 2D vs 3D shapes
description: Understand the difference between two-dimensional (lying in a plane, “flat”) and three-dimensional (“solid”) shapes.

skill: Analyze, compare, sort 2D/3D shapes
description: Analyze, compare, and sort two- and three-dimensional shapes, in different sizes and orientations, using informal language to describe their similarities, differences, parts, and other attributes. e.g., number of sides, number of vertices/“corners,” or having sides of equal length

skill: Model objects by building/drawing shapes
description: Model objects in their environment by building and/or drawing shapes. e.g., using blocks to build a simple representation in the classroom

skill: Compose larger shapes from simple shapes
description: Compose larger shapes from simple shapes. e.g., join two triangles to make a rectangle

skill: Make sense of problems and persevere
description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

skill: Reason abstractly and quantitatively
description: Reason abstractly and quantitatively.

skill: Construct viable arguments, critique reasoning
description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.

skill: Model with mathematics
description: Model with mathematics.

skill: Use appropriate tools strategically
description: Use appropriate tools strategically.

skill: Attend to precision
description: Attend to precision.

skill: Look for and make use of structure
description: Look for and make use of structure.

skill: Look for and express regularity in reasoning
description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
